title: How Much Money You Need for Coast FIRE in Different U.S. States
description: Geo-arbitrage and the cost of freedom across America.
content:
Coast FIRE is the point where you have saved enough in your retirement accounts that you no longer need to contribute another penny to retire comfortably at 65. This allows you to 'coast'—working just enough to cover daily bills, often switching to a lower-stress job. However, your Coast Number depends entirely on your spending. Reaching Coast FIRE in New York City requires a vastly different nest egg than in Mississippi. This guide calculates the specific targets for High, Medium, and Low cost-of-living states.

Key Takeaways

  • The Variables: Your number depends on 3 things: Your Age, Your Spending, and Your Retirement Age. Location drives the 'Spending' variable.
  • The HCOL Premium: You need ~2.5x more invested to Coast in California than in Arkansas due to housing and tax costs.
  • The Geo-Arbitrage Hack: The fastest path to Coast FIRE is to earn in a high-cost city, save aggressively, and then move to a low-cost state to 'Coast'.
  • Healthcare Factor: States with expanded Medicaid or robust ACA marketplaces make Coasting easier for early retirees.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Using the 'Rule of 72' and average market returns (7% real), money doubles roughly every 10 years. If you are 35 and want to retire at 65 (3 doubling periods), every $1 you have now is worth $8 then.

State-by-State Targets

Assumptions: Age 30. Retiring at 65. 7% Real Return. Target: $1.5M - $3M Nest Egg.

Tier 1: Low Cost (MS, AR, WV, AL)

Retirement Spend: $50,000/yr. Nest Egg Needed: $1.25M.

Coast Number at 30: $117,000.

Verdict: Highly achievable. If you have $117k at 30, you never need to save for retirement again in these states.

Tier 2: Medium Cost (TX, FL, NC, OH)

Retirement Spend: $75,000/yr. Nest Egg Needed: $1.87M.

Coast Number at 30: $175,000.

Verdict: Requires a solid decade of saving in your 20s.

Tier 3: High Cost (CA, NY, MA, HI)

Retirement Spend: $120,000/yr. Nest Egg Needed: $3M.

Coast Number at 30: $280,000.

Verdict: You are playing on Hard Mode. You need a high income to hit this early.

The 'Move to Coast' Strategy

  1. Phase 1 (Accumulation): Work in a Tier 3 city (NYC/SF). Earn $150k+. Live with roommates. Save $50k/year for 5 years. You hit $250k.
  2. Phase 2 (The Coast): Move to a Tier 1/2 state (NC/TN). Buy a cheap house. Take a job paying $60k that you enjoy (Non-profit, Park Ranger).
  3. Phase 3 (The Math): Your $250k grows to $2.5M by age 65 without you adding a dime. You live comfortably on your $60k salary. You have won the game.
  4. The Risk: If you move back to a HCOL city later, your math breaks. This is a one-way door strategy usually.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does this include Social Security?

No. These numbers rely purely on your portfolio. Social Security is the safety buffer that makes the plan even safer.

What if the market crashes?

Coast FIRE relies on long timelines (30+ years). A crash in year 2 doesn't matter. A crash in year 29 matters. You have time to recover.

Can I Coast with kids?

Yes, but your 'daily expenses' needed to Coast are higher (daycare/food). You need a higher paying 'Coast Job' to cover the bills.
